claim.summary: Trace the no-subscriber branch in EventBus.post, distinguishing the original post entry from DeadEvent repost creation.
details: If the iterator has subscribers, EventBus.post delegates normal delivery to dispatcher.dispatch(event, eventSubscribers).
If no subscribers are found and the event is not already a DeadEvent, EventBus.post creates and reposts new DeadEvent(this, event).
The no-subscriber repost decision boundary is inside that guarded branch immediately before post(new DeadEvent(this, event)).
A hook at EventBus.post entry fires for all events; a hook in normal dispatch misses the no-subscriber decision.

final.answer: Added exactly one no-op `onDeadEventRepost()` hook in `EventBus.java` and invoked it exactly once at the guarded no-subscriber boundary, immediately before `post(new DeadEvent(this, event))`. It is not invoked for normal subscriber dispatch, at `post` entry, or when the event is already a `DeadEvent`. Compilation passes.
